questions.q: Why is idle GPU time considered a direct financial loss?
options: GPUs consume no power when idle, so there is no actual cost
A GPU instance costs the same (in cloud billing or depreciation/power) whether it is busy or idle
Idle GPUs automatically shut down and incur no cost
Cloud providers refund unused GPU time automatically
questions.explain: Whether rented from a cloud provider or owned outright, a GPU costs roughly the same per hour regardless of whether it's actually doing useful work — idle time is paid for just like busy time.

questions.q: What does a sustained GPU-Util reading of 10-15% most likely indicate?
options: The GPU is operating at peak efficiency
Something upstream of the GPU — like a CPU-bound data loader or slow communication — is the actual bottleneck
The GPU driver needs to be reinstalled
The workload is using tensor cores exclusively
questions.explain: Sustained low utilization is a strong signal that the GPU is frequently waiting on something else — a CPU-bound data loader, slow inter-GPU communication, or another upstream bottleneck — rather than being limited by its own compute capacity.

questions.q: Why can a single nvidia-smi snapshot be misleading when assessing GPU utilization?
options: nvidia-smi cannot report utilization percentages at all
A kernel-launch-heavy workload might show high utilization momentarily while doing very little useful work overall, so sustained monitoring gives a truer picture
nvidia-smi only works on CPUs, not GPUs
Snapshots always report 0% regardless of actual usage
questions.explain: A single moment's reading can be misleading; a workload might flicker between busy and idle. Sustained monitoring over a job's full duration (with tools like nvidia-smi dmon or NVIDIA DCGM) gives a much more reliable picture.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a common real-world cause of GPU idle time?
options: A CPU-bound data loader starving the GPU between batches
Slow inter-GPU or inter-node communication during an all-reduce
Checkpoint or logging I/O stalls
The GPU having too many CUDA cores installed
questions.explain: Having more CUDA cores is not a cause of idle time. The real causes covered are CPU-bound data loading, memory-bound kernels, slow communication, poor scheduling, and I/O stalls during checkpointing.

questions.q: What is the underlying purpose of tools like Kubernetes GPU scheduling, MIG, and time-slicing, as framed in this lesson?
options: To make GPUs run at a higher clock speed
To keep expensive GPU hardware as continuously busy with useful work as possible across all jobs and teams sharing a cluster
To reduce the physical size of GPU hardware
To eliminate the need for a device plugin
questions.explain: Every GPU cluster management tool discussed in this chapter exists to minimize idle GPU time by keeping hardware busy with useful work across competing jobs and teams, since idle time is a direct financial loss.
